claim: Type II nuclear receptors (T2NRs) require heterodimerization with a common partner, the retinoid X receptor (RXR), to bind cognate DNA recognition sites in chromatin.
source: Type II nuclear receptors (T2NRs) require heterodimerization with a common partner, the retinoid X receptor (RXR), to bind cognate DNA recognition sites in chromatin.
evidence: This is a statement of established knowledge about T2NR function, supported by the broader scientific literature as indicated by the context of the manuscript.

claim: Based on previous biochemical and overexpression studies, binding of T2NRs to chromatin is proposed to be regulated by competition for a limiting pool of the core RXR subunit.
source: Based on previous biochemical and overexpression studies, binding of T2NRs to chromatin is proposed to be regulated by competition for a limiting pool of the core RXR subunit.
evidence: This claim references previous studies and represents the existing model in the field.

claim: The mechanism that binding of T2NRs to chromatin is regulated by competition for a limiting pool of RXR has not yet been tested for endogenous proteins in live cells.
source: However, this mechanism has not yet been tested for endogenous proteins in live cells.
evidence: This is a statement about the gap in existing research that the manuscript addresses.

claim: Higher expression of RAR, but not RXR, increases heterodimerization and chromatin binding in U2OS cells.
source: Unexpectedly, we find that higher expression of RAR, but not RXR, increases heterodimerization and chromatin binding in U2OS cells.
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study supported by experimental data from SMT and PAPA experiments.

claim: The limiting factor for RAR-RXR heterodimerization is not RXR but likely its cadre of obligate dimer binding partners.
source: This surprising finding indicates the limiting factor is not RXR but likely its cadre of obligate dimer binding partners.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the experimental findings presented in the manuscript.

claim: Dimerization between different members of a protein family can generate TF-TF combinations with distinct regulatory properties resulting in functional diversity and specificity.
source: Often, dimerization between different members of a protein family can generate TF-TF combinations with distinct regulatory properties resulting in functional diversity and specificity (Nandagopal et al., 2022; Puig-Barbé et al., 2023).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Switching of heterocomplexes between MYC/MAX and MAD/MAX results in differential regulation of genes and cell fate.
source: Several studies have shown that switching of heterocomplexes between MYC/MAX and MAD/MAX results in differential regulation of genes and cell fate (Amati et al., 1993; Bouchard et al., 2001; Hurlin and Huang, 2006; Xu et al., 2001).
evidence: This claim is supported by multiple citations to previous studies.

claim: T2NRs constitute an extensive group of basic leucine zipper TFs that share a common modular structure composed of a well-conserved ligand binding domain (LBD) that mediates heterodimerization with their obligate partner retinoid X receptor (RXR) and a highly conserved DNA binding domain that recognizes consensus sequences termed direct response elements.
source: T2NRs constitute an extensive group of basic leucine zipper TFs that share a common modular structure composed of a well-conserved ligand binding domain (LBD) that mediates heterodimerization with their obligate partner retinoid X receptor (RXR) and a highly conserved DNA binding domain that recognizes consensus sequences termed direct response elements (Evans and Mangelsdorf, 2014).
evidence: This is established knowledge about T2NR structure supported by a citation.

claim: Unlike Type I nuclear receptors, T2NRs do not depend on ligand binding for DNA engagement.
source: Unlike Type I nuclear receptors, T2NRs do not depend on ligand binding for DNA engagement.
evidence: This is a statement of established knowledge about T2NR function.

claim: Binding of ligands to the LBD of chromatin-associated T2NR heterodimers results in eviction of co-repressors and recruitment of co-activators.
source: Rather, binding of ligands to the LBD of chromatin- associated T2NR heterodimers results in eviction of co-repressors and recruitment of co-activators (Evans and Mangelsdorf, 2014; McKenna and O'Malley, 2002; Figure 1A).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations and illustrated in Figure 1A.

claim: Homozygous knock-in of HaloTag at the N-terminus of RXRα and the C-terminus of RARα was successfully generated using CRISPR/Cas9-mediated genome editing.
source: Using CRISPR/Cas9-mediated genome editing, we generated clonal lines with homozygous knock-in (KI) of HaloTag at the N-terminus of RXRα and the C-terminus of RARα (Heckert et al., 2022b; Los et al., 2008; Figure 1—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is a methodological claim supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1A.

claim: Western blotting confirmed that RARα and RXRα were tagged appropriately and expressed at similar levels to the untagged proteins.
source: Western blotting confirmed that RARα and RXRα were tagged appropriately and expressed at similar levels to the untagged proteins (Figure 1B)
evidence: This claim is supported by western blot data shown in Figure 1B.

claim: Co-immunoprecipitation experiments verified that Halo-tagged RARα and RXRα heterodimerize normally as expected.
source: while co-immunoprecipitation (co-IP) experiments verified that Halo-tagged RARα and RXRα heterodimerize normally as expected (Figure 1—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This claim is supported by co-IP experimental data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1B.

claim: The RAR ligand, all-trans retinoic acid (atRA), activated retinoic acid responsive element (RARE)-driven gene expression in wild-type and homozygously edited clones.
source: In addition, we confirmed using luciferase assays that the RAR ligand, all-trans retinoic acid (atRA), activated retinoic acid responsive element (RARE)-driven gene expression in wild-type and homozygously edited clones, confirming the normal transactivation function of the tagged proteins (Figure 1—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: This claim is supported by luciferase assay data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1C.

claim: Confocal live-cell imaging of cells stained with Janelia Fluor X 549 (JFX549) Halo ligand displayed normal nuclear localization of both Halo-tagged RARα and RXRα.
source: Confocal live-cell imaging of cells stained with Janelia Fluor X 549 (JFX549) Halo ligand displayed normal nuclear localization of both Halo-tagged RARα and RXRα (Figure 1—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: This claim is supported by confocal imaging data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1D.

claim: RARα and RXRα both exhibit a clearly separated slow diffusing population (<0.15 μm2/s) along with a faster mobile population (1–10 μm2/s).
source: We observed that RARα and RXRα both exhibit a clearly separated slow diffusing population (<0.15 μm2/s) along with a faster mobile population (1–10 μm2/s) (Figure 1C).
evidence: This claim is supported by single-molecule tracking data shown in Figure 1C.

claim: RARα has a chromatin-bound fraction (fbound) of 50 ± 3.0%.
source: In comparison with Halo H2B (fbound = 75.5 ± 0.7%) and Halo-NLS (fbound = 10 ± 0.9%), RARα and RXRα have intermediate levels of chromatin binding (fbound of 50 ± 3.0% and 38 ± 3.5%, respectively) (Figure 1D).
evidence: This is a quantitative measurement from SMT experiments shown in Figure 1D.

claim: RXRα has a chromatin-bound fraction (fbound) of 38 ± 3.5%.
source: In comparison with Halo H2B (fbound = 75.5 ± 0.7%) and Halo-NLS (fbound = 10 ± 0.9%), RARα and RXRα have intermediate levels of chromatin binding (fbound of 50 ± 3.0% and 38 ± 3.5%, respectively) (Figure 1D).
evidence: This is a quantitative measurement from SMT experiments shown in Figure 1D.

claim: The fbound was reproducible between three clonal cell lines of RARα (49 ± 1%, 47 ± 1%, 53 ± 1%).
source: The fbound was reproducible between three clonal cell lines of RARα (49 ± 1%, 47 ± 1%, 53 ± 1%) and RXRα (36 ± 1%, 36 ± 1%, 42 ± 1%).
evidence: This claim reports reproducibility of measurements across multiple clonal lines.

claim: The fbound was reproducible between three clonal cell lines of RXRα (36 ± 1%, 36 ± 1%, 42 ± 1%).
source: The fbound was reproducible between three clonal cell lines of RARα (49 ± 1%, 47 ± 1%, 53 ± 1%) and RXRα (36 ± 1%, 36 ± 1%, 42 ± 1%).
evidence: This claim reports reproducibility of measurements across multiple clonal lines.

claim: No significant change in fbound of RARα and RXRα was observed upon atRA treatment.
source: Finally, although recent studies have reported an increase in chromatin interaction upon agonist treatment (Brazda et al., 2014; Brazda et al., 2011; Rehó et al., 2023; Rehó et al., 2020), we did not observe a significant change in fbound of RARα and RXRα upon atRA treatment, nor did atRA treatment appear to alter the fast-moving populations of RARα and RXRα (Figure 1—figure supplement 3A and B).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 3A and B, and contrasts with previous studies cited.

claim: The results are consistent with the classic model in which dimerization and chromatin binding of T2NRs are ligand independent.
source: These results are consistent with the classic model in which dimerization and chromatin binding of T2NRs are ligand independent.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the experimental results in the context of existing models.

claim: Average cellular abundance of endogenous RARα and RXRα obtained from biological replicates of each homozygous clone were similar.
source: Average cellular abundance of endogenous RARα and RXRα obtained from biological replicates of each homozygous clone were similar (Figure 2B).
evidence: This claim is supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 2B.

claim: Expression of exogenous RARα-Halo was approximately four times that of the endogenous protein.
source: In contrast, expression of exogenous RARα-Halo was approximately four times that of the endogenous protein, while expression of Halo-RXRα was nearly twenty times that of endogenous RXRα (Figure 2B).
evidence: This is a quantitative measurement from flow cytometry shown in Figure 2B.

claim: Expression of Halo-RXRα was nearly twenty times that of endogenous RXRα.
source: In contrast, expression of exogenous RARα-Halo was approximately four times that of the endogenous protein, while expression of Halo-RXRα was nearly twenty times that of endogenous RXRα (Figure 2B).
evidence: This is a quantitative measurement from flow cytometry shown in Figure 2B.

claim: Chromatin binding of overexpressed RARα was reduced by approximately half compared to endogenous (fbound = 27 ± 0.72%).
source: Chromatin binding of overexpressed RARα was reduced by approximately half compared to endogenous (fbound = 27 ± 0.72%) (Figure 2C, Figure 2—figure supplement 1B)
evidence: This is a quantitative measurement from SMT experiments shown in Figure 2C and Figure 2—figure supplement 1B.

claim: Chromatin binding of overexpressed RXRα was decreased to 11 ± 0.75% - a value barely above the fbound of the Halo-NLS control.
source: while that of overexpressed RXRα was decreased even more dramatically to 11 ± 0.75% - a value barely above the fbound of the Halo-NLS control (Figure 2C, Figure 2—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This is a quantitative measurement from SMT experiments shown in Figure 2C and Figure 2—figure supplement 1B.

claim: A negative correlation was observed in single cells between TF concentration and fbound.
source: Using nuclear fluorescence intensity as a rough proxy for protein concentration in individual cells, we observed a negative correlation in single cells between TF concentration and fbound (Figure 2—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: This claim is supported by single-cell analysis data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1C.

claim: Chromatin binding of both RARα and RXRα in U2OS cells is saturable.
source: These results imply that chromatin binding of both RARα and RXRα in U2OS cells is saturable - i.e., the total number of chromatin-bound molecules does not increase indefinitely with expression level but is in some way limited.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the experimental data showing reduced fbound with overexpression.

claim: The fbound of endogenous RARα-Halo (47 ± 1%) was largely unchanged upon expression of RXRα-SNAP (49 ± 1%), consistent with the control SNAP (47 ± 1%).
source: Surprisingly, we found that the fbound of endogenous RARα-Halo (47 ± 1%) was largely unchanged upon expression of RXRα-SNAP (49 ± 1%), consistent with the control SNAP (47 ± 1%) (Figure 2F, Figure 2—figure supplement 4B)
evidence: This is a quantitative measurement from SMT experiments shown in Figure 2F and Figure 2—figure supplement 4B.

claim: RARα fbound is not limited by the availability of RXR.
source: implying that RARα fbound is not limited by the availability of RXR.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the experimental finding that RXRα overexpression does not increase RARα fbound.

claim: RARα-SNAP expression significantly decreased chromatin binding of endogenous RARα-Halo to 29 ± 5%.
source: In contrast, RARα-SNAP expression significantly decreased chromatin binding of endogenous RARα-Halo to 29 ± 5% (Figure 2F, Figure 2—figure supplement 4B).
evidence: This is a quantitative measurement from SMT experiments shown in Figure 2F and Figure 2—figure supplement 4B.

claim: Overexpression of mutant RARαRR-SNAP did not change the fbound of endogenous RARα (43 ± 4%).
source: However, overexpression of mutant RARαRR-SNAP did not change the fbound of endogenous RARα (43 ± 4%) (Figure 2F, Figure 2—figure supplement 4B)
evidence: This is a quantitative measurement from SMT experiments shown in Figure 2F and Figure 2—figure supplement 4B.

claim: Heterodimerization with RXRα is required for the effect of RARα overexpression on endogenous RARα fbound.
source: suggesting that heterodimerization with RXRα is required for this effect.
evidence: This is an interpretation based on the comparison between wild-type and mutant RARα overexpression effects.

claim: The initial fbound of endogenous Halo-RXRα (35 ± 1%) was barely altered by overexpression of SNAP (38 ± 1%) or RARαRR-SNAP (35 ± 1%).
source: In the reciprocal experiment with endogenous Halo-RXRα, the initial fbound (35 ± 1%) was barely altered by overexpression of SNAP (38 ± 1%) or RARαRR-SNAP (35 ± 1%).
evidence: This is a quantitative measurement from SMT experiments.

claim: Overexpression of SNAP-RXRα reduced the fbound of endogenous Halo-RXRα to 16 ± 2%.
source: As expected, overexpression of SNAP-RXRα reduced the fbound of endogenous Halo-RXRα to 16 ± 2%.
evidence: This is a quantitative measurement from SMT experiments.

claim: Overexpression of RARα-SNAP increased the fbound of endogenous Halo-RXRα to 56 ± 1%.
source: In contrast to RARα, however, overexpression of RARα-SNAP increased the fbound of endogenous Halo-RXRα to 56 ± 1%.
evidence: This is a quantitative measurement from SMT experiments.

claim: Endogenous RXRα chromatin binding is limited by the availability of RAR.
source: This result suggests that endogenous RXRα chromatin binding is limited by the availability of RAR (Figure 2F, Figure 2—figure supplement 4B)
evidence: This is an interpretation of the experimental finding that RARα overexpression increases RXRα fbound, supported by data in Figure 2F and Figure 2—figure supplement 4B.

claim: Endogenous RXRα is likely in excess while RXR partners are limiting in U2OS cells.
source: Notwithstanding these complexities, the results of the above SMT measurements in the presence of varying amounts of partner TFs allow us to infer that endogenous RXRα is likely in excess while RXR partners are limiting in U2OS cells.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the combined SMT experimental results.

claim: PAPA detects protein-protein interactions by using excitation of a 'sender' fluorophore with green light to reactivate a nearby 'receiver' fluorophore from a dark state.
source: PAPA detects protein-protein interactions by using excitation of a 'sender' fluorophore with green light to reactivate a nearby 'receiver' fluorophore from a dark state (Graham et al., 2022; Figure 3A).
evidence: This describes the PAPA method, supported by citation and illustrated in Figure 3A.

claim: Violet light is used to induce direct reactivation (DR) of receiver fluorophores independent of their proximity to the sender.
source: As an internal control, violet light is used to induce direct reactivation (DR) of receiver fluorophores independent of their proximity to the sender (Figure 3A).
evidence: This describes a control aspect of the PAPA method, illustrated in Figure 3A.

claim: A greater PAPA signal was seen for the Halo-RXRα → RARα-SNAP and RARα-Halo → SNAP-RXRα combinations than for the negative control, consistent with direct protein-protein interactions.
source: However, a greater PAPA signal was seen for the Halo-RXRα → RARα-SNAP and RARα-Halo → SNAP-RXRα combinations than for the negative control, consistent with direct protein-protein interactions (Figure 3B).
evidence: This is a finding from PAPA experiments shown in Figure 3B.

claim: The relation between DR and PAPA was sublinear for Halo-RXRα → RARα-SNAP and RARα-Halo → SNAP-RXRα combinations, consistent with saturation of binding to the Halo-tagged component.
source: The relation between DR and PAPA was sublinear (Figure 3B, left and middle panel, see residuals of the linear fit in Figure 3—figure supplement 1B), consistent with saturation of binding to the Halo-tagged component.
evidence: This is an analysis of PAPA data shown in Figure 3B and Figure 3—figure supplement 1B.

claim: The ratio of PAPA to DR for Halo-RXRα → RARαRR-SNAP was similar to the SNAP negative control, confirming that PAPA signal depends on a functional RAR-RXR interaction interface.
source: In contrast, the ratio of PAPA to DR for Halo-RXRα → RARαRR-SNAP was similar to the SNAP negative control, confirming that PAPA signal depends on a functional RAR-RXR interaction interface (Figure 3B, right panel).
evidence: This is a finding from PAPA experiments with the dimerization-incompetent mutant shown in Figure 3B.

claim: For both Halo-RXRα → RARα-SNAP and RARα-Halo → SNAP-RXRα combinations, PAPA trajectories had a substantially higher chromatin-bound fraction than DR trajectories.
source: For both Halo-RXRα → RARα-SNAP and RARα-Halo → SNAP-RXRα combinations, PAPA trajectories had a substantially higher chromatin-bound fraction than DR trajectories, indicating that a greater proportion of SNAP-tagged RARα/RXRα binds chromatin when it is in complex with its Halo-tagged partner.
evidence: This is a finding from PAPA-SMT experiments comparing PAPA and DR trajectories.

claim: Only a slight shift in bound fraction was seen for RARαRR-SNAP (fbound,DR = 7.5 ± 0.6%; fbound,PAPA = 11.1 ± 0.8%).
source: Only a slight shift in bound fraction was seen for RARαRR-SNAP (fbound,DR = 7.5 ± 0.6%; fbound,PAPA = 11.1 ± 0.8%), comparable to that seen for the SNAP negative control (fbound,DR = 7.1 ± 0.5% and fbound,PAPA = 11.2 ± 0.9% for Halo-RXRα; fbound,DR = 7.3 ± 0.4% and fbound,PAPA = 9.3±0.7 for RARα-Halo) (see Discussion)
evidence: This is a quantitative measurement from PAPA-SMT experiments.

claim: The enrichment of chromatin-bound molecules in the PAPA-reactivated population of both RAR and RXR is consistent with heterodimerization mediating chromatin binding.
source: The enrichment of chromatin-bound molecules in the PAPA-reactivated population of both RAR and RXR is consistent with heterodimerization mediating chromatin binding, that is further validated by the low fbound of the dimerization-incompetent mutant.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the PAPA-SMT experimental results.

claim: In U2OS cells, formation and chromatin binding of RAR-RXR heterodimers are limited by the concentration of RAR and not the core subunit RXR.
source: In stark contrast to the generally accepted T2NR competition model, our results reveal that in U2OS cells, formation and chromatin binding of RAR-RXR heterodimers are limited by the concentration of RAR and not the core subunit RXR (Figure 4).
evidence: This is a primary conclusion of the study supported by the combined experimental data and illustrated in Figure 4.

claim: PAPA-SMT directly confirmed in vivo that the association with RXRα promotes chromatin binding of RARα and vice versa.
source: PAPA-SMT directly confirmed in vivo that the association with RXRα promotes chromatin binding of RARα and vice versa (Figure 3C).
evidence: This is a finding from PAPA-SMT experiments shown in Figure 3C.

claim: Overexpression of RARα increases fbound of endogenous RXRα, while the reverse is not true.
source: However, unexpectedly, overexpression of RARα increases fbound of endogenous RXRα, while the reverse is not true (Figure 2F)
evidence: This is a finding from SMT experiments shown in Figure 2F.

claim: RXR is not limiting but is rather constrained by the availability of its binding partners.
source: indicating that RXR is not limiting but is rather constrained by the availability of its binding partners.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the experimental findings.

claim: The fbound of endogenous RARα (50%) and RXRα (38%) differed by about 10%.
source: Note that even though the number of RXRα and RARα molecules is about the same and the heterodimer complex has a predicted 1:1 stoichiometry (Rastinejad, 2022; Rastinejad et al., 2000), the fbound of endogenous RARα (50%) and RXRα (38%) differed by about 10% (Figures 1D and 2B).
evidence: This is an observation from the experimental data with reference to structural predictions from the literature.

claim: The difference in fbound between RARα and RXRα could be explained by expression of additional RXR isoforms (most likely RXRβ) in U2OS cells.
source: This surprising result could be explained by expression of additional RXR isoforms (most likely RXRβ) in U2OS cells (Figure 1A, Appendix 2—table 1, Figure 1—figure supplement 2B).
evidence: This is an interpretation of the experimental results with reference to expression data in Appendix 2—table 1 and Figure 1—figure supplement 2B.

claim: The fbound of overexpressed RARα decreases only twofold, even though it is in fourfold excess over endogenous RXRα, suggesting that there are other heterodimerization partners of RARα available.
source: The fact that the fbound of overexpressed RARα decreases only twofold, even though it is in fourfold excess over endogenous RXRα, likewise suggests that there are other heterodimerization partners of RARα available (Figure 2A and B, see Appendix 2—table 1).
evidence: This is an interpretation of the experimental data with reference to expression data in Appendix 2—table 1.

claim: The fbound of overexpressed RXR is essentially the same as the NLS control, indicating this excess core partner remains nearly totally unbound.
source: Moreover, the fbound of overexpressed RXR is essentially the same as the NLS control, indicating this excess core partner remains nearly totally unbound (Figure 2C).
evidence: This is a finding from SMT experiments shown in Figure 2C.

claim: Endogenous RXR is already in excess such that any additional RXR would remain mostly monomeric and unbound to chromatin.
source: This is consistent with endogenous RXR already being in excess such that any additional RXR would remain mostly monomeric and unbound to chromatin.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the experimental findings.

claim: Despite not directly measuring the protein levels of all RXR isoforms, we can still deduce in U2OS cells that RXR is in excess relative to its binding partners.
source: Hence, despite not directly measuring the protein levels of all RXR isoforms, we can still deduce in U2OS cells that RXR is in excess relative to its binding partners.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the combined experimental evidence.

claim: Overexpression of RARα significantly lowers the expression of endogenous RARα.
source: First, we find that overexpression of RARα significantly lowers the expression of endogenous RARα (Figure 2E)
evidence: This is a finding from flow cytometry experiments shown in Figure 2E.

claim: RAR participates in negative autoregulation at the transcriptional level or an excess of RAR causes instability at the protein level.
source: implying either that RAR participates in negative autoregulation at the transcriptional level or, that an excess of RAR causes instability at the protein level.
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation of the observation that RARα overexpression reduces endogenous RARα levels.

claim: Endogenous RAR may be more readily degraded when not bound by RXR, analogous to what was recently shown for the c-MYC/MAX heterodimers.
source: It is possible that endogenous RAR may be more readily degraded when not bound by RXR, analogous to what was recently shown for the c-MYC/MAX heterodimers (Mark et al., 2023).
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation with reference to a similar mechanism in another system.

claim: RARα expression decreases upon ligand treatment.
source: Second, as has been previously reported, RARα expression decreases upon ligand treatment (Ismail and Nawaz, 2005; Kopf et al., 2000; Osburn et al., 2001; Tsai et al., 2023; Zhu et al., 1999).
evidence: This is a statement of established knowledge supported by multiple citations.

claim: A 50% reduction in RARα upon addition of ligand did not affect the fbound of either RARα or RXRα.
source: Curiously, a 50% reduction in RARα upon addition of ligand did not affect the fbound of either RARα or RXRα (Figure 1—figure supplement 3A and B)
evidence: This is a finding from SMT experiments with ligand treatment shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 3A and B.

claim: Most chromatin binding of endogenous RXRα in U2OS cells depends on heterodimerization partners other than RARα.
source: suggesting that most chromatin binding of endogenous RXRα in U2OS cells depends on heterodimerization partners other than RARα (see Appendix 2—table 1).
evidence: This is an interpretation of the experimental finding that RARα reduction does not affect RXRα fbound, with reference to expression data in Appendix 2—table 1.

claim: An excess of RXR may ensure independent regulation of the different T2NRs without disrupting crosstalk between them.
source: Instead, an excess of RXR may ensure independent regulation of the different T2NRs without disrupting crosstalk between them (Figure 4).
evidence: This is a proposed model based on the experimental findings, illustrated in Figure 4.

claim: Competition for RXR between T2NRs may occur in some cases since different cell types express RXR and partner T2NRs in varying amounts.
source: Therefore, we cannot rule out that competition for RXR between T2NRs occurs in some cases since different cell types express RXR and partner T2NRs in varying amounts.
evidence: This is a speculative statement acknowledging limitations of the study.

claim: Chromatin binding by any given T2NR will likely depend on the concentrations of all other T2NRs.
source: It seems likely that chromatin binding by any given T2NR will depend on the concentrations of all other T2NRs.
evidence: This is a speculative inference based on the network nature of T2NR interactions.

claim: Dysregulation of T2NR expression has been reported in several types of cancers as well as other diseases.
source: especially since dysregulation of T2NR expression has been reported in several types of cancers as well as other diseases (Brabender et al., 2005; Collins-Racie et al., 2009; Frigo et al., 2021; Long and Campbell, 2015).
evidence: This is a statement of established knowledge supported by citations.

claim: SMT and PAPA-SMT provide one empirical way to determine which set of components in a dimerization network is stoichiometrically limiting in a given cell type, without having to measure the concentration of every T2NR or the affinity of every interaction.
source: Here, we have shown that SMT and PAPA-SMT provide one empirical way to determine which set of components in a dimerization network is stoichiometrically limiting in a given cell type, without having to measure the concentration of every T2NR or the affinity of every interaction.
evidence: This is a methodological conclusion of the study.

claim: The basic framework established here could be extended to probe the effect of ligands or small molecules on the T2NR interaction network or other dimerization networks seen in bHLH or leucine zipper family of TFs.
source: The basic framework we have established here could also be extended to probe the effect of ligands or small molecules on the T2NR interaction network or other dimerization networks seen in bHLH or leucine zipper family of TFs, providing useful information about critical regulatory network interactions often implicated in diseases.
evidence: This is a speculative statement about potential future applications of the methods.

claim: U2OS cells were grown in Dulbecco's modified Eagle's medium (DMEM) with 4.5 g/l glucose supplemented with 10% fetal bovine serum (FBS), 1 mM sodium pyruvate, L-glutamine, GlutaMAX, and 100 U/ml penicillin-streptomycin at 37°C and 5% CO2.
source: U2OS cells were grown in Dulbecco's modified Eagle's medium (DMEM) with 4.5 g/l glucose supplemented with 10% fetal bovine serum (FBS) (HyClone, Logan UT, Cat. #AE28209315), 1 mM sodium pyruvate (Thermo Fisher 11360070), L-glutamine (Sigma #G3126-100G), GlutaMAX (Thermo Fisher #35050061), and 100 U/ml penicillin-streptomycin (Thermo Fisher #15140122) at 37°C and 5% CO2.
evidence: This is a methodological description of cell culture conditions.

claim: Stable cell lines expressing exogenous gene products were generated by PiggyBac transposition and antibiotic selection.
source: Stable cell lines expressing the exogenous gene products (Appendix 2—table 2) were generated by PiggyBac transposition and antibiotic selection.
evidence: This is a methodological description.

claim: KI cell lines were generated using CRISPR/Cas9-mediated genome editing with sgRNAs designed using CRISPOR web tool.
source: KI cell lines were generated as previously described (Hansen et al., 2017) with some modifications. Halo-tagging of endogenous RARα was described in our previously published work (Heckert et al., 2022b) which we have further validated for the current study. For Halo-tagging we designed sgRNAs using CRISPOR web tool (Concordet and Haeussler, 2018).
evidence: This is a methodological description with citations to previous work.

claim: For RXRα tagging, exon 1 is very short (only 9 aa) so gene editing was performed at the start of exon 2 for successful tagging.
source: Since exon 1 of RXRα is very short (only 9 aa) we chose to gene edit at the start of exon 2 for a successful tagging.
evidence: This is a methodological decision based on the gene structure.

claim: Homozygous clones with the correct genotype (V5-Halo-RXRα clones C10, D6, and D9) were confirmed by Sanger sequencing and western blotting.
source: Homozygous clones with the correct genotype (V5-Halo-RXRα clones C10, D6, and D9) were confirmed by Sanger sequencing and western blotting.
evidence: This is a methodological description of validation procedures.

claim: All SMT experiments were performed using a custom-built microscope with a Nikon TI microscope equipped with a ×100/NA 1.49 oil immersion TIRF objective.
source: All SMT experiments were performed using a custom-built microscope as previously described (Hansen et al., 2017). Briefly, a Nikon TI microscope was equipped with a ×100/NA 1.49 oil immersion total internal reflection fluorescence (TIRF) objective (Nikon apochromat CFI Apo TIRF 100× Oil)
evidence: This is a methodological description with citation to previous work.

claim: All imaging was performed using highly inclined optical sheet (HILO) illumination.
source: All imaging was performed using highly inclined optical sheet (HILO) illumination (Tokunaga et al., 2008).
evidence: This is a methodological description with citation.

claim: To calculate fbound of RARα and RXRα with minimal bias and variation, at least 10,000 pooled trajectories from n≥20 cells are needed.
source: Note, we estimated that to calculate fbound of RARα and RXRα with minimal bias and variation, we need to analyze at least 10,000 pooled trajectories from n≥20 cells (Figure 1—figure supplement 1E).
evidence: This is a methodological determination based on subsampling analysis shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1E.

claim: The variance within collected SMT data was largely due to cell-to-cell variance.
